name: Carrion Defense Works Fragmentation Sleeve FS-2 'Shrapnel Hug'
description: A wearable explosive device disguised as an armored forearm sleeve, containing a directional fragmentation charge that detonates outward from the wearer's arm in a 120-degree cone. The FS-2 is a suicide-adjacent weapon designed for absolute last-resort scenarios — the wearer extends their arm toward a target and triggers the detonation, sending a spray of pre-scored tungsten fragments in a directed blast. The sleeve's inner surface contains a thin blast shield that protects the wearer's arm from the worst of the detonation, though burns and shrapnel wounds to the operator are expected. Carrion markets it as a 'final option personal defense system.'
specifications:
fragmentation cone: 120 degrees from arm axis
effective range: 2-8 meters
fragment material: Pre-scored tungsten cubes, 4mm
fragment count: approximately 200
blast shield: Inner ceramic layer, partial operator protection
weight: 0.8 kg
detonation: Neural trigger or manual switch
operator injury: Expected — burns and minor shrapnel to operator arm
story_hooks: A bodyguard detonated an FS-2 sleeve to protect their principal during an ambush — the bodyguard survived with a mangled arm, but the three attackers did not. The footage has gone viral.
Modified FS-2 sleeves with removed blast shields are being sold as improvised suicide weapons — the buyer does not survive, but neither does anyone within 8 meters.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist forearm gauntlet with a pronounced bulbous upper section containing the charge chamber. The silhouette is asymmetrical and menacing — sleek along the inner arm, bulging outward with visible segment lines indicating the fragmentation grid. Looks like a piece of armor that's been retrofitted with something far more lethal.
physical_description.dimensions: 32 cm length (wrist to elbow), 18 cm width at widest point (charge chamber), 12 cm depth. Barrel projection of charge axis approximately 8 cm forward from forearm axis.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and front-weighted — the charge chamber drags slightly but sits balanced enough for extended wear. Feels like strapping on a small siege weapon rather than armor.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced carbon-composite shell with internal titanium ribbing. Inner blast shield is layered ceramic-polymer composite (charred at service).
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial black with weathered brushed titanium accents around segmentation lines. Heat-stress discoloration visible on edges — browns and purples from repeated detonation cycles.
physical_description.color_scheme: Flat black primary with gunmetal gray segment seams and burnt-orange heat scarring. Faint QUANTA currency symbols etched near the detonation chamber in reflective ink.
physical_description.grip_texture: The inner arm contact is rubberized with aggressive hexagonal grip pattern. Manual detonation switch (if equipped) is knurled bare metal, slightly corroded.
distinctive_features: Visible tungsten fragment grid pattern embossed on outer surface showing pre-score lines
Thermal stress discoloration in concentric rings radiating from charge center
Three LED indicators (red/amber/green) mounted on inner wrist section for charge status
Micro-scarring and micro-fractures across ceramic inner lining from blast reflection
Directional vents along the 120-degree cone axis with sacrificial aluminum fins
Jury-rigged secondary manual detonation cable running along the interior (field modification common on Tier 3+ units)
Burn marks on the outer arm contact point where operator's skin contact left char patterns
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CARRION DEFENSE WORKS stamped in serif font on the charge chamber face. Serial number laser-etched into inner arm lining (often deliberately obscured by users). Small warranty void disclaimer under the charge access plate.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show significant wear — the inner ceramic is always scorched and micro-fractured. Outer carbon shell accumulates impact damage and thermal scars. Most street units are maintained but visibly abused; pristine examples are rare and suggest minimal activation history (which raises questions about the owner's survival rate).
